messages.subject: Shape fill?
parts:
When combining geom_line() with the shape=0 argument (or any other
open shape), the line goes over the open shape (see attached image
below). Is there a way to bring the geom_shape() layer to the top and
to make it opaque, so the line runs under it?

http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/web/transparentglyphs.png

Here's some sample code: -
myvar=c(1:10)
myd=data.frame(myvar)
ggplot(myd)+
theme_bw()+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(), panel.grid.major = theme_blank
())+
geom_line(aes(x=myvar,y=myvar))+
geom_point(aes(x=myvar,y=myvar),size=3, shape=0)

Hi thanks yes that did the trick! I actually tried to use
fill="white" with shape=0 (i.e. open square) and it didn't work. You
changed the shape to 22 (also apparently an open square) and it
worked. Could you please explain what the difference is between
shape=0 and shape=22? Can't seem to find any documentation on it on
the website or in the ggplot2 book. Thanks.
